subject: CHEMISTRY
title: Acid–base titration — standardisation of HCl
aim: Determine the concentration of an unknown hydrochloric acid solution by titrating it against 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide.

hazards.name: Corrosive acid & alkali
hazards.text: Wear lab coat, safety goggles, and gloves when handling HCl and NaOH solutions.

hazards.name: Glassware breakage
hazards.text: Clamp the burette securely in the retort stand and use a funnel only while filling.

procedure: Complete the pre-lab PPE and hazard check before entering the bench.
Rinse the burette with a little HCl, fill it, remove the funnel, and record the initial reading to 0.05 cm³.
Pipette 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH into the conical flask and add 2–3 drops of indicator.
Perform one rough titration, swirling continuously over the white tile until the end point.
Refill and run accurate titrations, switching to dropwise flow near the end point until two accurate titres agree within 0.10 cm³.
Compute the mean concordant titre and calculate the molar concentration of HCl.

precautions.text: Read the lower meniscus at eye level to avoid parallax error.
Removed the funnel from the burette before starting the titration.
Swirled the conical flask continuously and added acid dropwise near the end point.
Rinsed the burette with acid and pipette with base, and flushed out air bubbles from the jet.

glossary.titre: Volume of titrant delivered from the burette (final reading minus initial reading).
glossary.concordant: Two accurate titres that agree within 0.10 cm³.
glossary.equivalence point: Point at which stoichiometrically equal moles of acid and base have reacted.
